html:
A tall grain crop domesticated in the western Sahel of West Africa about 4,500 years ago. It is now the most widely grown millet in the world.

As the Sahara dried out after about 3000 BCE, herders and foragers on its southern edge began to sow and harvest a wild grass. Over centuries they selected plants whose seeds stayed on the head instead of scattering, and whose grains grew larger. The result thrives where little else will: in heat, on sandy, poor soils, with little rain.

Pearl millet spread across Africa's dry belt and became a staple for porridge, beer and flatbread. It travelled east too, along with sorghum, and reached India by about 2000 BCE, part of the movement told under millets from Africa. In India it is called bajra and is still a main grain in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

It is one of several crops first farmed in West Africa, alongside African rice, cowpeas and yams. These crops fed the farming villages and later the cities of the Sahel, such as Djenné-Djenno.
sum: A tall grain crop domesticated in the western Sahel of West Africa about 4,500 years ago. It is now the most widely grown millet in the world.
